recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not loosen Timing.repeat.when for this issue; future work should be limited to separately approved additions of true recurring timing codes or extension guidance as later WG decisions describe.
issue_request: FHIR-13385 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 and asked for Timing.repeat.when to support more approximate day-period timing concepts. The accepted resolution changed the short and definition, added NOON plus early/late morning/afternoon/evening EventTiming codes, and required definitions to make the vague institutional/patient-interpretation semantics clear rather than making the code-typed element extensible.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites svn revision 12712, and git commit 7b39e2dc1b7999233017d71b8bc8ab9950775620 (#13385 - enhancements to Timing.repeat.when) made the corresponding source/datatypes/timing.xml changes. The current source still contains the requested short definition, expanded definition, and EventTiming code additions.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps normal datatype content in the active datatypes build scope. Later no-change decisions FHIR-17283 and FHIR-34124 revisited requests to loosen the same Timing.repeat.when binding and reaffirmed that the code datatype/required binding should not be made extensible or preferred; true missing timing codes should be proposed individually or handled with extensions. Zulip and Confluence records align with this interpretation and do not reveal a conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source files were changed because the current authoritative Timing datatype spreadsheet already carries the approved FHIR-13385 wording and code-list changes. The published commit is an empty audit record documenting that no further core-source edit is needed.

related_jiras.note: Later STU3 no-change request to loosen Timing.repeat.when, resolved Not Persuasive because event triggers are separate from recurring timing codes.
R5 re-raise of the binding-loosening request, resolved Not Persuasive with rationale that code type/normative status prevent relaxing the required binding.
